title: Julian day
summary: 1 January 2000 at 12:00 UT is Julian day 2451545. revJul turns that day back into the calendar date.

title: A Date in UTC
summary: Pass the date as year, month, day, and hours from midnight UT. TypeScript also accepts a Date, read in UTC. Date.UTC by itself is a count of milliseconds, so wrap it in new Date.

title: Delta T
summary: Delta T is TT minus UT, in seconds. Around the year 2000 it is about a minute.

title: Tropical Sun
summary: On this date the Sun is in Capricorn, within a degree of the ecliptic, and moves about one degree a day. Longitude, latitude, and speed are degrees. Distance is astronomical units.

title: Equatorial Sun
summary: Right ascension and declination are the equatorial place of date. A parallel aspect uses these. In January the Sun's declination is about 23° south.

title: Separation on the circle
summary: sep is the shortest arc on the circle, in degrees, from 0 to 180. From 10° to 350° that arc is 20°, not 340°. A longitude separated from itself is 0.

title: Lahiri sidereal Sun
summary: A sidereal longitude is the tropical longitude minus the ayanamsa. Lahiri with true nutation is the offset a Swiss-compatible chart subtracts. The whole-sign order is set on the same call. It does not move the Sun.

title: Mean nutation
summary: Mean nutation leaves the nutation in longitude inside the sidereal place. The two Suns differ by that nutation, a fraction of an arcminute, not by a new zodiac.

title: Citra and Galactic center
summary: True Citra and Lahiri both put Spica at the sidereal zero, so on this date they sit about an arcminute apart. Galactic center (Mula) is a different zero: the projected right ascension of Sgr A* at the middle of Mula, several degrees from Lahiri. All three values include nutation in longitude.

title: Inclined Lilith
summary: The default mean Lilith sits on the mean lunar orbit. Its latitude reaches about 5.15°.

title: Ecliptic Lilith
summary: Ecliptic Lilith keeps the same longitude and sets the latitude to 0. A declination taken from that point is not the latitude of the orbit.

title: Placidus
groupIntro: The houses below are for 1 January 2000, 12:00 UT, at 50.22° N and 18.67° E, unless the story names another latitude.
summary: For Placidus, cusp 1 is the ascendant and cusp 10 is the midheaven. The cusp array starts at 0, so cusp 1 is index 0. At an ordinary latitude fallback stays false.

title: Equal houses
summary: Equal houses step 30° from the ascendant. They are not snapped to the start of a sign.

title: Whole sign, shift then snap
summary: Subtract the ayanamsa from the ascendant, then snap to a sign. The cusps fall on 0° of the sidereal signs. This chart uses Lahiri and true nutation.

title: Whole sign, snap then shift
summary: Snap the tropical ascendant to a sign, then subtract the ayanamsa. The cusp leaves the sign boundary by the remainder of the ayanamsa.

title: ARMC stays put
summary: ARMC is the right ascension of the meridian, a time angle. Sidereal mode does not shift it. The ascendant does move.

title: Right ascension stays put
summary: Sidereal mode subtracts the ayanamsa from ecliptic longitude. Right ascension stays the apparent place of date.

title: Sripati
summary: Sripati puts each cusp in the middle of a Porphyry sector. The ascendant is still an angle of the chart, and it is not a cusp.

title: Polich-Page
summary: In Polich-Page the ascendant is cusp 1 and the midheaven is cusp 10.

title: Inside the polar circle
summary: At latitude 80° a quadrant house cannot always be formed. Placidus and Koch then use Porphyry and set fallback.
